sentences.text: Sunlight looks white. So why is the sky blue?
Light travels in waves, and blue waves are shorter than red ones.
When sunlight hits the air, tiny gas molecules scatter it in every direction. And blue is scattered more than the other colors.
NOAA says blue scatters about four times more strongly than red. That's why blue is what we see most of the time.
Near the horizon, the sky fades to a lighter blue or white. That light has passed through even more air, scattering again and again.
At sunset the light takes an even longer path. The air scatters more of the blue wavelengths than the orange and red, and that gives the golden glow.
So, if the sky is basically sunlight getting bounced around... is it showing off its color, or just really bad at keeping light in one place?
